web_evidence.title: The Cuckoo’s Calling — Book Extract
web_evidence.note: The official Robert Galbraith site’s sustained ten-page extract narrates Robin and Strike externally, shifting focalization between them while consistently retaining third-person narration.

web_evidence.title: Extract: The Cuckoo's Calling by Robert Galbraith
web_evidence.note: The published opening prologue uses nonparticipating third-person narration for the death scene and ensuing press reaction.

web_evidence.title: The Cultural Criminology of The Cuckoo’s Calling
web_evidence.note: Rafe McGregor’s published scholarly book chapter analyzes the novel’s complete structure and explicitly identifies its narration as third person, mostly focalized through Strike and occasionally Robin.

web_evidence.title: Robert Galbraith Writing Styles in The Cuckoo's Calling
web_evidence.note: The study guide’s point-of-view section explicitly describes the whole novel as third-person narration following the thoughts and actions of Strike and Robin.

person_note: The diagnostic Goodreads passages repeatedly render Strike externally and disclose his thoughts in third person, especially q02103, q02107, q02111, and q02114. Many shorter event quotations were conservatively left unmarked because a bare name or third-person pronoun cannot alone establish the controlling narrator. First- and second-person forms elsewhere are dialogue, gnomic address, or unresolved quotation material. Independent Tier A extracts show third-person narration across the prologue and opening chapters, including shifts between Robin and Strike, while the Tier B whole-book analysis explicitly confirms third person throughout. No evidence supports sustained first- or second-person base sections; the only material limitation is that the authorized prose excerpts cover the opening rather than every part of the novel.
